issue.description: During unrelated commit-finalizer retry-loop verification on 2026-09-06, just check escalated to the governed full pytest lane (core-identity-changed) and failed this node once in a 38,856-item parallel run. The local diff touched finalizer code/tests, not agents_sync. Immediate unchanged rerun of both failed nodes with .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q passed: 2 passed in 5.39s, with this node taking 0.26s call time after setup. The broad run's retained temp log was truncated before the failure traceback, so the exact assertion still needs confirmation.

task_type_fields.evidence: Failed once under the governed full parallel lane reached by just check escalation on 2026-09-06, then passed immediately on an unchanged isolated rerun. The test uses a real 30s blocked render with a 0.2s drain timeout and an elapsed < 5.0 assertion, so investigate whether host load can exceed the wall-clock budget or whether publication drain cleanup can occasionally stall.

payload.entry:
RESOLVED sase-xo - the bounded-drain publication flake (test_blocked_render_is_bounded_and_leaves_the_request_queued). Fixing commits: sase 3e6c19ee37 + sase-core f061f5f6 (Rust enforces recovery and caller deadlines; exception cleanup shares one one-second budget across both regenerable path families and every git subprocess/recovery attempt), plus this tale's landing repair (host-finalized in the closeout turn, no SHA cited here): the cleanup cap is now the required Rust policy with no Python 1.0 fallback or independent cap, and a policy lookup failure attaches to the original publication exception without running cleanup. BEFORE: injected index-lock contention (blocked render + owner-free sidecar .git/index.lock) measured 15.6448s elapsed / 14.6253s cleanup, matching the 15.63s fleet report. AFTER (phase .2): 2.41s young-lock case, 2.08s stalled-cleanup case, 1.25s original case, 9 bounded-drain tests + 20 core git-lock tests. AFTER (this turn, final tree): 12 of 12 concurrent runs of the bounded-drain + cleanup-policy modules (26 tests each, 12 processes with 4 xdist workers each, 16 busy loops) passed, young-lock case 2.43-2.50s and stalled-cleanup case 2.06-2.08s against the unchanged 5.0s bound; the elapsed bound, queued-request, later-retry and lock-release assertions are untouched. New regressions prove a missing/raising binding is exposed, the original exception and timeout attribution survive, and a smaller Rust cap bounds a stalled cleanup. sase check c3d751031ae96ebbfdca08ab1cfe32bc and sase-core check 141fcdc410d4549d8645dce189f6a0ab both succeeded.

FOLLOW-UP DISPOSITIONS (lander FOLLOW-UP TRIAGE, carried into this close): (1) sase-1qt.1 note 4 wheel-cache proposal DECLINED as a cache bug: cache key 86beb74a9a2d2d03ad7707e25660b915fd68d290bdf38141e327d120e4664d50 metadata names a CLEAN core b0a63dc3 (wheel sha256 9f33941aa12e...), which predates agent_prompt_select in 45c6a260, so the missing binding is expected; the cache refuses dirty trees and rechecks source identity after build, and no incorrect exact-identity hit was shown. (2) sase-1qt.2 notes 2 and 3 are ONE drain-accounting test-order issue (cold 9 failed/3 passed, 12/12 with sase.core.git_lock_facade preloaded), retained and routed as a DISCOVERED ISSUE to active global-state epic sase-j7 (.2/.4); no duplicate task was created. (3) The import-budget proposal (sase-1qt.2 note 3, referenced by notes 4/5) is RESOLVED as this epic's own integration work: cleanup contributed +3,036 eager bytes and clan navigation +2,269 against the unchanged 12,162,484 cap; fixed by deferring the agents_sync tree, now 11,893,483 bytes (epic note #3). Phase .3 proposed no follow-up; adjacent sase-15e and sase-15f stay separately owned and untouched.

CORRECTION (2026-11-02 redo): The earlier note citing root check c3d751031ae96ebbfdca08ab1cfe32bc and core check 141fcdc410d4549d8645dce189f6a0ab describes verification on the prior tale workspace whose implementation was subsequently lost before host finalization; those runs do not prove the redo tree. Current redo evidence: linked sase-core check 4a9213fc94c163648a869096d3f07bd9 passed, and root check bfa36032ec65f99c78566f3df4a1a3a8 passed after the final lazy-import test patch corrections. No check-full was run. The Rust-owned cleanup bound and current publication-policy regressions are recorded on reopened epic sase-1qt.
